j.name: Li Mei
j.line: Welcome to the Jade Market! We have everything from the finest jade to rare cultivation scrolls.
lines: Make sure to visit the Pavilion of Rest for some refreshments.
The Sparring Platform is the best place to test your skills against other disciples.
j.persona: Li Mei is a friendly merchant who runs a jade shop in the Jade Market.

n.name: Jade Merchant Ling
n.line: Welcome to the Jade Market, where the finest treasures of the Nine Heavens are exchanged.
lines: Please, take your time to browse through our offerings and find what your heart desires.
Remember, a wise buyer is one who knows the value of a true gem.
n.persona: A seasoned merchant at the Jade Market, known for her keen eye for rare artifacts.

m.name: Zhen
m.line: Greetings, traveler. Welcome to the Jade Pagoda, a place of learning and spiritual growth.
lines: May I ask what brings you to our hallowed halls?
The Sparring Platform is the best place to test your skills against others.
m.persona: A resident of the Jade Pagoda, Zhen is a dedicated martial artist who spends most of his time in the Pavilion of Rest and the Sparring Platform.

p.name: Master Yun
p.line: Welcome to the Jade Pagoda, seeker of truth and power. May your steps be light and your heart pure.
lines: The Courtyard of Falling Water is where many find peace and clarity, do not miss it.
The Sealed Scripture Room holds ancient knowledge, but be wary of the guards.
p.persona: A sage and guardian of the Jade Pagoda, known for his wisdom and guidance to those who seek enlightenment.

q.name: Lan Feng
q.line: Welcome to the Jade Market, dear traveler. What brings you to our bustling heart?
lines: Looking for jade? Our market has the finest stones from the Nine Provinces.
May the fortune of the Jade Pagoda bless your journey.
q.persona: A cheerful merchant in the Jade Market, known for her knowledge of jade and its properties.

K.note: a sealed chest someone in The Jade Pagoda hoped nobody would find

R.title: The Pagoda's Foundation Stone
R.text: Nine tiers for nine virtues, built downward, because the first abbot said a sect should grow toward its trials, not away from them.
